steps.text: I'll confirm the sizes first. The 80 mm and 100 mm come from your request. The wall, base, and honeycomb sizes are my guesses, so please check them.

dims.label: Hexagon across corners
dims.note: Taken as corner to corner; say if you meant flat to flat

dims.label: Side wall thickness
dims.note: Typical for a pen cup that holds its shape

dims.label: Honeycomb cell, corner to corner
dims.note: Hex holes cut through each side wall

steps.text: The sizes are confirmed. Next I'll set out the build plan, since this part has several features.

assumptions: 80 mm is corner to corner (across corners), so the hexagon has corners on the X axis
Walls 2 mm, base 3 mm, open top
Honeycomb cells run through all six side walls, staggered rows from z 15 to 80, leaving the base and rim solid
Cells are hex prisms 10 mm corner to corner with 2 mm ribs between them
questions: Is 80 mm across corners or across flats? I assumed corners.
Should the honeycomb stop short of the rim, or reach the top?

steps.text: The plan is approved. I'll start building the hexagon body.
The hexagon came out with corners on the Y axis, not X as planned. I'll undo it and rotate the sketch 30 degrees.
The body now has corners on X and matches the plan. Next I'll cut the cavity from the top, leaving a 3 mm base.
The cavity is cut and the body is 80 by 100 mm. Now the honeycomb: I'll cut one face of cells at a time, starting with the +Y wall.

The cut ran, but the volume is about half of what the honeycomb should remove, and I found the cause. The `circumscribed` fit makes the 80 mm the across-flats distance, not across corners. I'll undo the three steps and rebuild with `inscribed`, which puts 80 mm across the corners.
The body is now 80 mm across the corners on X, with flats at ±Y. Next the cavity, sized inscribed at 75.4 mm so the walls stay 2 mm.
The cavity checks out: 3 mm base and 2 mm walls. Now the honeycomb on the +Y wall, using the same cell layout.
The +Y wall removed about 2,590 mm³, which matches the expected 2,600. Now the other five walls, one at a time.
All six walls are cut, and the volume drop matches six walls of cells. Now I'll check the part against the plan.

The pen cup is built and the sizes are right: 80 mm across the corners, 69.3 mm across the flats, 100 mm tall, watertight, with 2 mm walls. The honeycomb has 20 cells on each of the six walls, cut through and leaving the base and rim solid.

**The plan check failed on one item.** The plan expected 3 features, and the part has 8 steps: body, cavity, and six wall cuts for the honeycomb. The geometry matches the plan, so I did not change it. Say if you want the honeycomb merged into fewer steps, or if the 8-step build is fine.

The 80 mm was taken as corner to corner, and the wall, base, and cell sizes are my guesses. I have not sliced or queued anything. Should I send it to your P1S on a 0.6 mm nozzle in PLA?
